newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close mixed in very quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close mixed in very quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed in very quiet trade on Monday amid a lack of significant economic news, with investors looking ahead to auction results and economic reports due out this week and next, analysts said.

"We've just sort of held in. We've got a little bit of momentum follow through from last week," said Rich Wylie, a fixed-income economist with TD Securities Inc. "Now we're going to be looking for the budget next week."
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.15 to C$111.80 to yield 7.010 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 30 basis points from 31 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

Canadian bonds moved in a tight range as Canadian economic reports on housing starts and raw material prices had little impact on prices. With a light calendar of economic data for the remainder of the week, Canadian bonds investors are now expected to turn their focus to Canada's federal budget being released on February 18, analysts said.
Bond investors are also expected to focus on bond auctions this week in both Canada and the United States.

The success of three U.S. refunding auctions, which will sell almost US$40 billion in bonds, is expected to help set the tone for North American fixed-income markets this week. In Canada, the federal government will auction C$2.3 billion in new bonds on Wednesday.

In other news, a Standard & Poor official said the rating agency is unlikely to upgrade Canada's foreign currency credit rating in the near future despite the country's improved financial situation. However, the agency said it is considering changing the outlook on its AA+ rating to stable from negative.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.03 to C$104.78 to yield 6.335 percent.
The U.S. bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.41 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to eight basis points from five basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.82 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.13 percent.
